id: title:danielcarletti:let resume cdc through a self managed lag marker

review.posthog_relevance: Adds a classification marker for CDC recovery, potentially distinguishing recoverable self-managed lag from broken sources, though the backend implementation and recovery behavior are not shown.
review.reason: Adds a new constant and its registration, imports it, and modifies the resume endpoint to exclude this marker from broken-source rejection. This could prevent unnecessary repair routing for recoverable lag, but the implementation of the marker and recovery is not shown.
review.uncertainty: The chunk does not include the implementation of the SELF_MANAGED_LAG_REASON constant or the backend logic that sets this marker, only its registration and its use in the resume endpoint and tests. This makes it impossible to distinguish whether this is a new capability or a maintenance of an existing marker, and to assess the systemic risk reduction or broader capability.

observations.behavior: Adds a new constant SELF_MANAGED_LAG_REASON and its registration in the error reason mapping.
observations.posthog_connection: Adds a new reason value to the CDC repair error classification, potentially distinguishing a recoverable self-managed lag from a broken source.

observations.behavior: Imports the new constant into the CDC resume view.
observations.posthog_connection: Makes the new constant available for use in the resume endpoint, but does not show how it is used.

observations.behavior: Changes the resume endpoint to exclude markers with reason SELF_MANAGED_LAG_REASON from the broken-source rejection, allowing them to proceed to recovery.

observations.posthog_connection: Allows CDC recovery to proceed for markers classified as self-managed lag, while still rejecting other broken markers. This could prevent unnecessary repair routing for recoverable lag, but the implementation of the marker and recovery is not shown.
